innerTube.title: Inner Tube System
innerTube.description: The classic standard: a tire paired with an inner tube. The pneumatic tube sits inside the outer tire.
innerTube.label: Universal Compatibility

tubeless.title: Tubeless System
tubeless.description: No inner tube is required. The tire, specialized rim, and valve create a sealed air chamber similar to an automotive tire.
tubeless.label: Performance Standard

suitability.title: Is Tubeless For Me?
suitability.innerTube: If you ride for daily commuting or casual leisure, inner tubes are sufficient and low maintenance.
suitability.tubeless: If you ride on rough terrain, want lower rolling resistance, or need advanced puncture protection, tubeless is the stronger choice.
suitability.note: If you previously used an aluminum rim with a traditional inner tube and tire setup and now plan to upgrade to tubeless, first check the rim cross-section diagram above. Rims designed for tubeless compatibility can support both inner tube setups and tubeless tires. If your rim matches the first example, designed only for standard inner tube use, it is not compatible with tubeless tires and must be replaced.

selfSealing.title: Self-Sealing
selfSealing.description: Sealant can fill small punctures automatically. No pinch flats from an inner tube.

lowerPressure.title: Lower Pressure
lowerPressure.description: Hooked road setups can run around 80 psi or lower for better grip and comfort without pinch flats. Hookless rims with tubeless tires have an absolute ceiling of 73 PSI / 5.0 bar; follow any lower manufacturer limit.

rollingResistance.title: Rolling Resistance
rollingResistance.description: Removing friction between tube and tire can improve rolling speed.

pressure.title: Pressure Check
pressure.description: Check tire, rim, load, and source-limit inputs
